x: Alpaquitay AI is a free, open-source (MIT) extension for Visual Studio Code. It puts a harness between your intent and your code: it picks the right route for each request, shows you every change as a diff before writing it, checks the gates of the software lifecycle and keeps a local record of what happened. You can use it with models on your own machine (Ollama, LM Studio or its WebGPU local engine) or with Anthropic and OpenAI. This manual explains how to use each part, what it is good for and what it guarantees, with screenshots and videos of the real extension. [!NOTE] Some messages inside the extension are in Spanish (for example the download confirmation and the progress notifications of the local engine). This manual quotes them as they appear and translates them.

Nothing is written without you seeing it. In the Hub, every code change first arrives as a bounded diff, and writing needs your si aplicar. (The exception is the classic Generate from Spec command, which writes directly; see Work.) Evidence before autonomy. Code tasks move to Done only with no pending diffs, an onboard-verified platform contract and green build/test evidence. Docs-only projects need no contract or build/test evidence, but pending diffs still block Done. Privacy by architecture. There is no Alpaquitay intermediary server. Local models never leave your machine; cloud calls go straight to your provider after passing a privacy boundary that hides personal data and secrets. Everything is recorded in your repository, in the .alpaquitay/ folder: decisions, debt, session economy, project memory and ADRs.
In five minutes you will have the extension installed, an AI provider connected and the Hub open on your project.

You need Details Visual Studio Code 1.85 or later (Windows, macOS or Linux). It also works in compatible editors that install from Open VSX, such as VSCodium. An open folder The harness works on the workspace folder: it analyses it, writes spec.md there and keeps its evidence in .alpaquitay/. Git (recommended) DORA signals, the traceable history and the checkpoints before writing use Git. Without Git the extension works, but without those three things. An AI provider Local (Ollama, LM Studio, local engine) or cloud (Anthropic, OpenAI). You choose it in chapter 2.

h: Your first session, step by step
x: Open a project folder in VS Code (File → Open Folder). It can be a new project or a legacy one. Connect a provider. The quickest private option is Ollama: install it and run ollama pull qwen2.5-coder (or any model). Alpaquitay finds it on its own at http://localhost:11434. More options in chapter 2. Open the Hub with <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdAlt</kbd+<kbdA</kbd. Type onboard in the chat of the Work tab. It is free (no model call): it analyses the project, detects the build and test commands, writes a first ADR and computes the DORA signals. See Chat commands. Create your spec with + Create with AI in the Spec pane, or with the Generate Specification (Local Model) command if nothing may leave your machine. Drag a task to In Progress and review the diff it proposes. Type si aplicar to write it or no to discard it. [!TIP] If no provider is configured, the chat says so: «No hay proveedor AI disponible. Configura uno en ⚙ o inicia Ollama/LM Studio.» (no AI provider available; configure one or start Ollama/LM Studio). The harness commands that use no model (dora, deuda, economía, postmortem) also need an active provider in this version, because they are typed in the same chat.

h: What is created in your project
x: Alpaquitay only writes inside your workspace folder, and almost everything inside .alpaquitay/: File Content spec.md Your spec: epics and tasks. It is the board's source of truth. .alpaquitay/decisions.jsonl One line per harness decision: route, lane, confidence and reasons. .alpaquitay/debt.json The agentic debt meter and its latest events. .alpaquitay/economy.json Model calls versus free local operations. .alpaquitay/fingerprint.json, platform.json The detected stack and the build and test commands. .alpaquitay/ADR-001-onboard.md, .alpaquitay/adrs/ Architecture decision records. .alpaquitay/memory.json Hierarchical project memory (classes, functions, completed tasks). .alpaquitay/ideas.json The inbox of ideas that are not tasks yet. You decide whether to commit .alpaquitay/: sharing it gives the team the same decision history; ignoring it keeps it personal.

Uninstall from the Extensions view. The .alpaquitay/ folder and spec.md stay in your project (they are yours); delete them by hand if you do not want them. If you used the local engine, first run Alpaquitay AI: Clear Local Model Cache to free the space of the downloaded model.
Alpaquitay has no cloud model of its own and never routes your data through a server of its own. You choose who answers: a model on your machine, or a cloud API that the extension calls directly.

Models under about 4 billion parameters (names with 1.3b, 3b, mini, nano, gemma:2b…) are detected by name. For them Alpaquitay uses shorter, stricter instructions, lowers the temperature and strips the filler comments they tend to add. Even so, for tasks that touch several files a 7B model or larger gives clearly better results.

When a request goes to a cloud provider, it first passes the privacy boundary (PrivacyBoundaryProvider): It detects and replaces personal data (emails, phone numbers, ID numbers, cards, IBANs, IP addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers) and secrets (credentials, bearer tokens, private keys, provider API keys, AWS keys, JWTs) with placeholders. It sends the cleaned request straight to your provider. It returns the reply exactly as the provider wrote it. Placeholders are not reversed: if the reply quotes a value that was hidden, you will see the placeholder instead. It records metadata only: how many replacements and of which kind, never the detected values. The record is written before the call, so failed requests are audited too. The Evidence tab shows the boundary's state (the Privacy boundary card): telemetry, replacements and where the keys are stored. [!IMPORTANT] The privacy boundary lowers the risk, but it does not anonymise your code: the source code itself is sent to the cloud provider you choose. If your code must not leave your machine, use a local provider.
alpaquitay-ai.enableTelemetry is false. If you turn it on, only anonymous usage statistics are sent; never code or prompts. Details are in the privacy policy.

In Settings → Global Defaults: Setting Default Effect Max output tokens 4096 Reply limit when the provider has none of its own. Temperature 0.3 0 = deterministic, 2 = creative. For code, stay between 0 and 0.4. It is sent to local models and to cloud models that accept it; Alpaquitay does not send it to current reasoning models. Request timeout 120,000 ms Maximum time per request. Raise it for slow local models. System Prompt empty Instructions added to every request (for example, your team's conventions). Organization context empty Your team's name or context, to tailor the answers.

A plain AI assistant takes your text and answers. Alpaquitay puts a harness in front: a deterministic layer (no model involved) that perceives the project, decides what kind of work this is, limits what can happen and keeps a record. Knowing how it works helps you ask better and understand why it sometimes asks before acting.

Perceive. It detects the stack from marker files (package.json, pom.xml, go.mod, pyproject.toml…) and the real source folders. It never assumes the code lives in src/. Decide. It classifies your request into a lane and a lifecycle phase, with a visible confidence and reasons. Preview. If something must be written, it prepares a bounded diff. Nothing touches the disk yet. Guard and verify. Write policy, automatic review, a Git checkpoint and, after applying, the real build and test commands. Keep evidence. Decisions, debt and economy are stored in .alpaquitay/.

One call, or none. 🔨 Build Create, implement, fix or refactor; talk about the spec or the board. From the board: plans, generates and leaves pending diffs for you to approve. From the chat: once you confirm with si, it turns your request into a new spec.md to work through on the board (see the warning below). 2 to 4 calls per confirmed change. 🧠 Deep The message mentions deployment (deploy, despliegue), pipelines, Docker, Terraform, AWS, Azure, GCP, IaC, DORA, pentests, threats (amenazas), STRIDE, SBOM, OWASP SAMM, FinOps, zero trust, runbooks or MLOps. Sends the request to one registered specialist (security, DevOps, architecture, QA…). One call to the specialist. The harness decides with readable rules, not with another model. h: The six SDLC phases and their gates
x: The harness also places each request in a lifecycle phase. A phase only moves on when its exit gate passes. Phase Triggered by words such as… Exit gate 01 Requirements requisito, idea, alcance, historia, objetivo, épica objective + scope + out of scope + owner 02 Design diseño, arquitectura, ADR, diagrama, esquema ADR recorded + no circular dependencies 03 Implementation crea, genera, implementa, fix, bug, refactor, endpoint SOLID + preview + checkpoint + build and test 04 Testing test, prueba, coverage, QA, e2e, unit happy path + edge + error for every public method 05 Deployment deploy, pipeline, docker, release, rollback, terraform, aws green pipeline + human approval + rollback ready 06 Maintenance logs, deuda, upgrade, incidente, postmortem, oncall runbook + alert + service owner

Letter Principle How you notice it F Fingerprint-first It detects your real stack before proposing anything. A Ask-before-act Every write and every risky route asks for confirmation. B Bounded preview A change plans at most 6 files; more than that must be split into batches. L Legible-first Every answer states lane, stack, phase, gate and economy. E Evidence-always Every decision lands in .alpaquitay/decisions.jsonl.

Review agent activity and diffs in Changes. Its Apply & run gates and Discard all buttons act on every pending diff; applying starts the same guarded flow as si aplicar, and discarding is equivalent to no. When you reply si aplicar (or click Apply & run gates), for each pending file: Write policy. Files that are secrets are always denied: .env, .pem, .key, idrsa, ided25519, secrets/ folders, credential or token files. Writing spec.md needs confirmation and a backup. Automatic review (no model). It blocks when the file is outside the detected source folders or the content looks like a literal secret (API keys, private keys, AWS keys, sk-…, ghp…, JWTs). It warns when the file passes 400 lines, when console.log, print(, TODO or FIXME remain, or when the change changes nothing. Git checkpoint. Before writing it saves a stash named alpaquitay/apply-diffs-<date and re-applies it, so your work stays in the tree and you also get a way back. Without Git it carries on without a checkpoint and says so. Write and verify. It writes the approved files and runs the real build and test commands detected by onboard. To go back after a si aplicar, find the stash with git stash list (Alpaquitay's sta

A card moves to Done only when it passes the DoD gate: no diffs are left unapplied (si aplicar or no first); for code projects, the platform contract is verified by an explicit onboard run and saved for the current stack; for code projects, build and tests really ran and came back green. Knowing which command to run does not count as having run it. Projects with no source code (for example, only PDFs, Markdown and HTML) skip the contract and quality evidence checks; pending diffs still block Done. The gate reads the saved contract without creating one and runs the exact build and test commands stored in .alpaquitay/platform.json. If the stack is not detected, confirm both commands with onboard {"build":"...","test":"..."}. If something fails, the card stays In Progress and the chat shows what blocks it, with an automatic, blameless postmortem.

Every risky decision adds debt and every gate passed pays some back. The meter runs from 0 to 100; at 100 the Build lane is blocked until you pay it down. Event Points Pending diff left unresolved +2 Postmortem (something failed) +10 DoD blocked +15 Deployment without a rollback plan +25 Any other recorded decision +1 Successful si aplicar −5 Verified Done −8 onboard −10 Above 70 the harness warns you (alta, revisa antes de seguir: high, review before going on). Check the meter with deuda in the chat or in the Evidence tab.

The harness counts how many operations it solved locally, for free (dora, deuda, postmortem, diff, reviews, economía) against how many model calls it made. Type economía to see it. Its advice: short questions in Flash, onboard once, diffs in batches.

h: Where to look if you want to audit
x: Everything is text in your repository. decisions.jsonl has one JSON line per decision, with its route, lane, confidence and reasons; debt.json keeps the last 50 debt events. You can read them, commit them or process them with your own tools.

The Work tab is where the coding happens. It has three panes: the spec (spec.md), the Kanban board derived from it and the chat with the harness. This is Alpaquitay's SDD (spec-driven development) flow: first agree on what, then implement task by task, and every change stays linked to a requirement.

Under the tabs, the next-step bar follows the SDD flow, Spec → Build → Review → Verify, and shows one primary button for what to do now: Where you are The bar says The button No spec.md yet Start with a spec Create spec with AI Tasks waiting Next task: … Start SPEC-00x (prioritizes in Todo and starts work in In Progress) The AI is working AI is building … Watch progress Diffs pending Review N pending changes Review changes and Apply & run gates Debt at its ceiling Build is blocked by technical debt See debt Every task done All N tasks are done Validate against spec Every card in Backlog, Todo and In Progress also has a Start (or Resume) button, so dragging is optional. Above the chat input, quick buttons run Build next task, Validate, Tests and Refactor; when diffs are pending, Review and apply and Discard changes appear. Shortcut Action <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdK</kbd (<kbdCmd</kbd+<kbdK</kbd on macOS) Open the command palette: every tab, action and agent, searchable <kbdAlt</kbd+<kbd1</kbd to <kbd7</kbd (<kbdOption</kbd on macOS) Switch tab <kbd/</kbd Focus the chat

spec.md is plain Markdown at the root of your project, and it is the board's database: card state is read from this file, not stored elsewhere. So you can edit it by hand, review it in a pull request and version it like any other file. Format rules: A Title and a paragraph of context at the top. Each Epic: … (or any level-2 heading) groups tasks. - [ ] text is a pending task; - [x] text a finished one. The IDs SPEC-001, SPEC-002… are assigned by position. Free text between tasks is used as context for the AI. Does your project use another name, such as tasks.md or backlog.md? Change it in Settings → Workspace → Spec file (alpaquitay-ai.specFile). If the file does not exist, Alpaquitay looks for similar ones.

Generate Specification (Local Model) Your description must not leave your machine. It writes specs/<name.md and never overwrites. Command Palette or <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdA</kbd. See Local engine. By hand You already know what you want. Any editor. Click ↻ in the Spec pane to reload. [!TIP] A good spec has small, verifiable tasks that start with a verb: "Validate the email in the sign-up form" beats "Users". The AI implements a task of a couple of files far better than a whole epic.

Every pending task starts in Backlog. The usual flow is Backlog → Todo → In Progress → Done: move a task to Todo to prioritize it, then press Start to begin. Review happens within In Progress; it is not a fifth column. Starting a card from Todo (or moving it to In Progress) starts the AI, and it writes nothing blindly: Plan. The chat in the right pane understands three kinds of message: Natural language. The harness picks the lane (Flash, Build or Deep), shows its decision and asks for confirmation when needed. See How the harness thinks. Harness commands, such as onboard, dora, deuda or si aplicar. Most of them use no model calls. They are all in Chat commands. Skills, with the /skill button: create a file, refactor, generate tests, the daily standup… See Agents.

h: Ideas that are not tasks yet
x: Type a messy idea ("I have an idea: members could book with priority…"). The harness recognises the Flash · ideate lane and files it in the idea inbox (.alpaquitay/ideas.json) with a proposed objective, scope and out-of-scope. When it is clear, type promover and the latest idea becomes a new epic in spec.md.

Mention the task in the commit message: Both SPEC-001 and [SPEC: 001] are recognised. The Evidence tab marks those commits in the history and counts them in the repository signals: the more linked commits, the better the traceability.

h: Generate from Spec and Validate Against Spec
x: Besides the board, the quick menu has two classic commands that work with any spec file (.md, .yaml, .yml, .json or .feature): Generate from Spec picks a file, plans the files it needs and generates them. Validate Against Spec compares the project's code with the spec and reports what does not comply. [!WARNING] Generate from Spec writes the files directly, with no diff and no si aplicar, and can overwrite files with the same name. Use it on a clean Git tree so you can review the result with git diff and undo it if needed. For reviewed work, use the board. New Specification creates a template in specs/: REST API (OpenAPI 3.0), BDD feature (Gherkin), database schema, Spring Boot microservice or React component.

Besides natural language, the chat in the Work tab understands a set of short commands. Type them on their own, as the whole message. Most of them are solved on your machine without calling any model, so they are free and fast. The command names are Spanish words; type them exactly as shown.

Command What it does Calls a model? onboard Analyses the project, detects build and test, writes ADR-001 and computes DORA. No dora DORA signals from the last 40 commits. No deuda (debt) Shows the agentic debt meter. No economía or economia (economy) Local operations versus model calls in the session. No postmortem <text Classifies a failure you paste (build, test, lint, write…). No diff <path Shows a file's pending diff in full. No si aplicar (yes, apply) Writes every pending diff with policy, review and a checkpoint. No no Discards every pending diff. No promover (promote) Turns the latest idea in the inbox into an epic of spec.md. Yes si (or sí, dale, ok, confirmo) Confirms the route the harness proposed. Depends on the route [!NOTE] The chat needs an active provider to accept messages, even for these local commands. If there is none, you will see «No hay proveedor AI disponible» (no AI provider available).

Running onboard saves the contract verification; detecting a stack alone does not open the gate. For an unknown stack, confirm the commands with onboard {"build":"build command","test":"test command"}. The best first step in any project, especially a legacy one. Locally, it produces: Project fingerprint: frameworks, real source folders and entry points. It never assumes src/. Platform contract: the test, build and lint commands for your stack (stored in .alpaquitay/platform.json). If it cannot confirm them it says so (sin verificar — confirma tu comando: unverified, confirm your command). ADR-001: a first decision record with the stack, the sources and the harness rule (every write goes through diff, policy and checkpoint), in .alpaquitay/ADR-001-onboard.md. The repository's DORA level. It also removes 10 debt points. Run it once when you start, and again if your stack changes.

Computes delivery signals from git log (the last 40 commits), with no external telemetry: Signal How it is computed Frequency 15 or more commits: "daily or better"; 6 or more: "weekly"; fewer: "occasional". Lead time "Traceable by SPEC" when commits are linked to tasks. Failure rate Share of commits that are fix, hotfix, revert, rollback or bug. Recovery Through the harness checkpoints (stashes). Level High when at least 60% of commits are linked and the failure rate is ≤ 15%; Low when the rate is above 30%; Medium otherwise. [!IMPORTANT] These are repository-derived proxies, not operational DORA metrics: Git does not know when you deploy or when there is an incident. Alpaquitay labels them that way on purpose. Improve the signal by linking commits with SPEC-xxx and with fewer hotfixes.

Shows the score (0 to 100), a bar and the status: sana (healthy), alta — revisa antes de seguir (high, from 70) or techo roto — paga deuda antes de Build (ceiling broken, from 100). The point rules are in How the harness thinks.
Counts the operations solved locally (free) against model calls. Each confirmed Build costs 2 to 4 calls. Useful when you pay per use for a cloud provider.

Paste a failure after the word: It classifies it (build, test, lint, diagnostics, write or unknown), suggests the likely cause and the next step, with your project's test command. It runs nothing. The harness also writes an automatic, blameless postmortem when a board task fails.

You can also click Apply & run gates or Discard all in the Changes tab. Both buttons act on every pending diff; Apply & run gates runs the same reviews, checkpoint and gates as si aplicar. After the agent generates changes, the chat lists the pending diffs. Nothing is written yet. diff src/bookings/calendar.ts shows that file's full diff. si aplicar writes all pending files. First it checks the debt ceiling and that the folder is writable, saves a Git checkpoint and passes each file through the policy and the automatic review. A blocked file is not written; the rest are. no discards them all.
Takes the latest idea in the inbox (.alpaquitay/ideas.json) and adds it to spec.md as an epic with tasks. Since it writes spec.md, it first checks the folder and saves a checkpoint.
When the harness is unsure, or the route is Deep (a specialist), it proposes the route and waits. Reply si to go ahead with it; anything else is treated as a new message.

The Docs tab is for everything that is not code: manuscripts, reports, articles, documentation and books. You talk to the agent in English or Spanish, as you would to an editor: "proofread chapter 3" · "make it more direct, keep my voice" · "translate the book to Spanish" · "check consistency across chapters" · "what is this chapter missing?"

Format Read Write Notes .docx (Word) ✅ ✅ Edits are written as Word tracked changes (Review → Accept/Reject). Untouched paragraphs stay byte-identical. .md / .txt ✅ ✅ Lossless outside the edited blocks; code blocks, tables and front matter are protected. .epub ✅ ✅ Chapters follow the book's spine; italics and bold survive a round trip. .pdf ✅ ➡️ .md Read-only, best effort (text-based PDFs). A scanned PDF needs OCR first. From the same tab you can convert any document to Markdown, Word or EPUB: a manuscript in Markdown becomes a publishable EPUB in one click.

Open a document with Open file… or pick it from Documents in this workspace…. Choose an action or type your own instruction: Edit: Proofread (spelling and grammar), Improve style, Shorten, Translate to (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian or Portuguese). Analyse: Summarize, Outline, Consistency check (names, dates, places and terminology across chapters) and Editorial feedback. Review the proposal. Every changed paragraph shows a word-level diff. Large rewrites, changed numbers and big length changes are flagged review and are not pre-selected. Select with Select all, Only safe or None, or box by box. Click Apply selected. By default a new file is written (name.edited.docx, name.edited.md…). If you choose to overwrite, a backup is saved first in .alpaquitay/backups/. Verification. The written file is read back to check that it opens and contains every accepted edit. Analyses (summary, outline, consistency, feedback) do not change the document: save them with Save report as .md.

h: The same guarantees as for code
x: The agent only proposes; you decide what is applied. Protected blocks it never touches: links, footnotes, fields, images, tables and code. Whole books: if an operation needs more than 20 model calls it asks you first (Continue), and it never makes more than 60. Privacy: with a cloud provider the text goes through the privacy boundary (personal data and secrets hidden); with a local model the manuscript never leaves your machine. No external dependencies: the ZIP, DOCX, EPUB and PDF readers and writers are built in, so the extension stays small and auditable.

In a Word paragraph the agent rewrites, the formatting inside that paragraph (a bold word, for example) is replaced by the formatting of its first run. Tracked changes show exactly what changed. Paragraphs with hyperlinks, fields or notes are skipped rather than risk damaging them. Quality depends on the model. In our tests a 3B local model (llama3.2:3b) wrote a useful editorial report, but answered "No changes needed" when asked to fix a Spanish text with missing accents. To proofread, restyle or translate, use a 7B model or larger, or a cloud one. [!TIP] For a book, start with Consistency check and Outline: they change nothing and give you the big picture. Then proofread chapter by chapter with Proofread and take your time with the changes flagged review.

The Evidence tab is the delivery control panel: one screen with what the harness knows about your project and what is waiting for your decision. Its motto sums up Alpaquitay's idea: evidence before autonomy.

Card What it shows Repository signal The approximate DORA level computed from Git (High, Medium, Low or no data). Agentic debt Current debt out of 100. Review queue How many files have a diff waiting for your decision. Session economy Local operations versus model calls. The Run onboarding (same as onboard) and ↻ Refresh evidence buttons are at the top right.

The six phases (Requirements, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, Maintain) with their gate and state: routed, enforced, evidence, human gate or tracked. They show what kind of control the harness applies in each phase: in Build and Design it is enforced, in Test real evidence is required and in Deploy a person always decides. Details in How the harness thinks.

Lists every file with a pending diff. Two buttons: Discard all — discards them all (like no). Apply & run gates — applies them all with policy, automatic review and checkpoint, and runs build and test (like si aplicar). When the queue is empty you will see "No pending changes. The harness writes only after review."

The repository's latest commits, with a mark on those that link a task (SPEC-001 or [SPEC: 001]). The note next to it is deliberate: the DORA figures are repository-derived proxies; connect your real deployment and incident events before treating them as operational measurements.
Score, state (healthy, high or ceiling broken) and the latest events that moved it. At 100 the Build lane is blocked. It is paid down with onboard, applied diffs and verified Done tasks.

A reminder of the three lanes: Flash — local reception: questions, ideas and free commands. Build — diff-first implementation: plan, preview, apply and verify. Deep — one registered specialist: security, QA, architecture, DevOps… Every route leaves a receipt in .alpaquitay/decisions.jsonl: one agent, one receipt.

The session's privacy status: Line Usual value Telemetry Off by default Cloud redaction Boundary ready, or the number of replacements made in the latest cloud request Keys VS Code SecretStorage Intermediary servers None The harness strip (below the tabs) shows the same status in short: privacy on-device with a local provider and privacy cloud boundary with a cloud one.

The Architecture tab is an architecture canvas that starts filled in: Alpaquitay derives the system from what your project already has and from what the spec says will be built. Then you can edit it, ask for changes in plain language, document decisions and export infrastructure as code.

The inference is deterministic and local (no model). It reads: Dependencies in package.json (root and sub-packages) and other manifests: pom.xml, requirements.txt, go.mod, .csproj… docker-compose services: names and images (for example postgres, redis, rabbitmq). Folder names at the first and second level (api/, web/, worker/…). spec.md: what the project will build, with its epics as modules. With that it places at most 14 system nodes and 8 epic modules. Each node remembers its origin: the current workspace, the spec or an epic.

Add nodes from the palette: Compute (Lambda, Container, Service), Network (API Gateway, CDN, Client), Data (Database, Storage, Queue, Cache) and Security (Auth). Connect: <kbdShift</kbd+click the source node, then <kbdShift</kbd+click the target. Select: click (its properties appear on the right). Move: drag. Delete: select and press <kbdDelete</kbd. C4 level: the Context, Container and Component buttons mark the level you are working at. In this version they do not filter the diagram: every node shows at all three levels. For a C4 diagram by level, ask the architecture specialist in the chat ("generate a C4 container diagram of this project"). Save stores the diagram in .alpaquitay/arch.json; Clear empties it; ↻ Re-infer rebuilds it from the project even if one is saved.

h: Local engine: AI on your machine with WebGPU
x: [!NOTE] Available from version 3.6.1 of the extension. The local engine runs a language model inside VS Code, on your own GPU. Your text never leaves the machine: the only network traffic is a one-time download of the model files, which are signed. After that it works offline, and the server-side inference cost is zero.

Requirement Details WebGPU in VS Code A GPU with an up-to-date driver. The default model also needs the shader-f16 feature. Recent integrated GPUs (for example Intel UHD/Iris) work. Memory At least 8 GB of RAM. Disk About 1.3 GB for the default model's cache. Network Only the first time (or when a new model revision is published). If your machine misses any of these, the command refuses before downloading anything and tells you why.

Open a project folder. Select text in the editor describing what you want to specify, or select nothing. Run Alpaquitay AI: Generate Specification (Local Model) from the Command Palette (<kbdF1</kbd) or the <kbdCtrl</kbd+<kbdShift</kbd+<kbdA</kbd menu. If you selected nothing, type the description in the box («Describe el proyecto o la funcionalidad que quieres especificar (se procesa en tu equipo)»: describe the project or feature; it is processed on your machine). A request written in English produces a spec in English. The first time, confirm the download (see the next section). Follow the progress in the notification: runtime check, download, caching, loading on the GPU and token-by-token generation with its speed. The result is written to specs/<name.md in the same format the Work tab reads. It never overwrites an existing spec: if the name is taken, it adds -2, -3… You can cancel at any time from the notification.

Before downloading anything, VS Code shows a modal dialog: .") It shows the model and its license, the verified download size and these guarantees: integrity is checked against a signed manifest before any file is used, and your text is never sent to the CDN. In English: «Alpaquitay: el motor local necesita descargar el modelo.» — the local engine needs to download the model. «La integridad se verifica con un manifiesto firmado antes de usar cualquier archivo.» — integrity is verified against a signed manifest before any file is used. «Tu texto nunca se envía a la CDN: la inferencia ocurre en tu equipo.» — your text is never sent to the CDN; inference happens on your machine. Then: Descargar y generar (download and generate) starts the download. Cancel (or <kbdEsc</kbd) stops the command: nothing is downloaded and nothing leaves your machine. [!IMPORTANT] The dialog needs your click. With VS Code's default setting (window.dialogStyle: native) it is an operating-system dialog: a separate window that may open away from where you are looking. Until you answer, the notification stays on «Preparando motor local…» (preparing the local engine). If you see that and nothing happens, look fo

Measured on 15 November 2026 on a laptop with an Intel UHD (gen 9) integrated GPU, VS Code 1.146, from the production CDN, with the default model: Phase Time Downloading and verifying 1.26 GB about 3 minutes at ~7 MB/s (depends on your connection) Caching and loading on the GPU about 15 seconds Generation 4.5–4.7 tokens/s; a spec with 3 epics in ~45 s Later runs no download: just loading and generation [!NOTE] This is a 1.5-billion-parameter model. It writes good first drafts of specs; it does not replace a large model. If the result does not follow the spec.md format, the command warns you so you can review it.

h: Using it as an AI provider
x: Besides the command, the engine can be one more provider, like Ollama. In Settings → AI Provider, select Alpaquitay AI · Qwen 2.5 (on-device) and enable the engine. On first use, confirm the signed model download; VS Code shows progress and required disk space before using it. Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B runs on your machine, and your prompts are never sent to the CDN. With preferredProvider set to auto, it is used after Ollama and LM Studio. Keep its size in mind: it is fine for questions, ideas and specs; for multi-file tasks a larger model in Ollama or the cloud gives better results.

Files are stored in VS Code's own cache (the engine panel's IndexedDB), in 8 MiB blocks. A half-finished download is never used. When the model revision changes, the old weights are deleted automatically. Alpaquitay AI: Clear Local Model Cache empties the cache completely.

h: Security: why you can trust what is downloaded
x: The CDN is treated as untrusted by design. What makes a file valid is its signature, not the server: Every model has a manifest.json signed with Ed25519. The extension ships the project's public keys and refuses any manifest not signed by them, or older than the last one it saw (rollback protection). The manifest lists a SHA-256 for every 8 MiB block of every file. A changed byte, an unlisted file or a block that does not match is refused. The ONNX Runtime files are pinned by hash inside the extension itself, and the engine panel cannot load remote scripts. The manifest is downloaded without decompression: no decompressor parses network bytes before the signature check. The CDN address, the model and the trusted keys can only be changed in your user settings, never in a project's: a repository you open cannot redirect the download. You can check for yourself which models are published and whether their signature is valid in Available models.

Setting Default Purpose alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.enabled false Use the engine as an AI provider. The command works even when it is off. alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.modelId qwen2.5-coder-1.5b-instruct Which model to use (see Models). User settings only. alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.device auto auto, webgpu or wasm (CPU). alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.dtype auto Weight precision. Change it only if you see corrupted output. alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.maxNewTokens 1024 Maximum new tokens per generation. alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.cdnBaseUrl https://alpaquitay.specsolid.com CDN the models are downloaded from. User settings only. alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.extraTrustedKeys [] Extra public keys for your own CDN mirror. User settings only.

The engine's messages are in Spanish; here they are with their meaning. Message or symptom What it means What to do Stuck on «Preparando motor local…» The confirmation dialog is waiting for your answer. Find it in the taskbar and answer it. «VS Code está en renderizado por software…» (software rendering) VS Code's GPU process failed and Chromium switched to software rendering. Close every VS Code window and open it again. code --status must show webgpu: enabled under GPU Status. «la GPU (…) no concede un adaptador WebGPU» (no WebGPU adapter) The driver or Chromium's blocklist prevents WebGPU. Update your graphics driver. «este VS Code no expone la API navigator.gpu» VS Code is too old. Update VS Code. «Este modelo requiere WebGPU…» (this model requires WebGPU) Without WebGPU this model would be unusably slow on the CPU (single thread). Fix WebGPU with the rows above. «La GPU se quedó sin memoria o falló durante la generación» (GPU out of memory) The GPU had no memory for that request. The model is released. Close other apps using the GPU, shorten the description and try again. «Memoria agotada al cargar el modelo: reintentando en un panel nuevo» (out of memory, retrying in a new pa

This page queries the local engine's CDN (alpaquitay.specsolid.com) right now, downloads each published model's manifest and verifies its Ed25519 signature in your browser with the same public keys the extension ships. If a manifest were tampered with, you would see invalid signature here, just as VS Code would refuse it. [!NOTE] Checking Ed25519 signatures in the browser needs a recent version (Chrome or Edge 137+, Firefox 129+, Safari 17+). Older browsers show "your browser cannot verify Ed25519": that does not mean the model is wrong, only that this browser cannot check it. The extension always checks it.

h: How the default model was chosen
x: Every candidate was tested with the real extension, in an isolated VS Code, on the same laptop (Intel UHD gen 9 integrated GPU) and with the same Spanish request, served from a local CDN with a test key. Model License Download In VS Code Spec quality Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B Instruct (q4f16) ✅ Apache-2.0 1.26 GB 3.3–4.8 tok/s The best: concrete engineering tasks, SPEC-NNN, epics, in Spanish Gemma 3 1B (q4) Gemma Terms of Use (use restrictions) 0.82 GB 5.9 tok/s Weak: a single epic, no SPEC-NNN, content errors Qwen3 1.7B Apache-2.0 1.43 GB ❌ does not load — Granite 4.0 1B Apache-2.0 1.19 GB ❌ garbage output or does not load — Gemma 4 E2B Apache-2.0 3.2 GB ❌ too large — Conclusions: Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B is the only code-specialised candidate that works in the WebGPU runtime, and the one that wrote the best specs. Its license (Apache-2.0) does not restrict use. On this class of machine the engine does not load models above about 1.3 GB; that is why models that look better on paper (Qwen3, Gemma 4) are out for now. Gemma 3 1B is still published and can be chosen with alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.modelId: "gemma-3-1b-it"; it is faster but gives worse results. The full method, the files and the two
In your user settings (not the project's): Next time you run the command you will see the confirmation dialog with the new model's size. To go back to the default, delete the setting.

When the project publishes a new revision (corrected files or an optimised graph), the manifest carries a new revision and a higher sequence. The extension notices, asks you to confirm the new download and deletes the old weights. It never accepts a sequence lower than one it has already seen.

h: Publishing a model on your own CDN
x: To serve models from your own infrastructure (for example on a network without Internet access), the process is: prepare the graph, stage, sign with your key, upload and verify. Add your public key to alpaquitay-ai.localEngine.extraTrustedKeys and point cdnBaseUrl at your CDN. Full guide: worker/README.md and docs/LOCAL-ENGINE.md §6–7.
Each recipe says who it is for, what you need and the steps, with links to the chapter that explains each piece.

For: whoever inherits a repository and needs to find their way before touching anything. You need: the repository with its Git history, and any provider. x: Raise alpaquitay-ai.requestTimeout (for example to 300000) and, in Settings → Ollama, Max output tokens. On machines without a dedicated GPU, use a smaller model.

That is the DoD gate doing its job. The chat says what blocks it: «N diff(s) sin aplicar» (unapplied diffs) → reply si aplicar or no. «contrato platform sin verificar — corre onboard primero» (platform contract not verified) → run onboard and confirm the test command if asked. Build or tests failed → read the postmortem in the chat, fix it and try again.

h: *«Build bloqueado por techo de deuda»* (Build blocked by the debt ceiling)
x: Debt reached 100. Pay it down: onboard (−10), apply or discard the pending diffs and close tasks with evidence (−8 each). Check the status with deuda. Details

The policy or the automatic review stopped a file: Secret files (.env, .pem, .key…) are never written by the harness. Edit them yourself. Fuera de fuentes evidenciadas (outside the evidenced sources) means the file is outside the detected source folders. If the folder is right, run onboard again to refresh the project fingerprint.

h: I want to undo a `si aplicar`
x: A checkpoint was saved before writing: git stash list shows one named alpaquitay/apply-diffs-<date. Discard unwanted changes with Git (for example git restore <file) or bring back the checkpoint state with git stash apply stash@{N}.

h: My whole `spec.md` changed after a `si` in the chat
x: You confirmed a code request typed in the chat, which generates a new spec.md from the request. A checkpoint was saved first; get the previous version back with git stash list (look for alpaquitay/code-<date or alpaquitay/spec-<date) and git checkout stash@{N} -- spec.md, or with git checkout -- spec.md if it was committed. To keep it, add new tasks to the board instead of asking for them in the chat. Details

h: The board does not show my tasks
x: Is your spec called spec.md and at the root? If not, change alpaquitay-ai.specFile. Do the tasks use the - [ ] text format under a heading? Format Click ↻ in the Spec pane to reload.

h: The local engine does not work
x: The full table of messages and fixes is in Local engine → If something goes wrong. The two most common causes: The confirmation dialog is waiting for your click out of sight. Look for it in the taskbar. VS Code is rendering in software after its GPU process failed. Close all its windows and open it again; check with: GPU Status must show webgpu: enabled.

h: A cloud model answers with a 400 error
x: Current Claude and GPT models reason before answering and reject some older request parameters. From version 3.6.1 Alpaquitay only sends temperature to models that accept it and uses maxcompletiontokens with OpenAI. If you use an older version, choose a model from the selector or update the extension.

That shortcut is also GitHub Copilot's. Alpaquitay uses it for its quick menu, which includes an entry to open Copilot Chat. To use another shortcut, change it in File → Preferences → Keyboard Shortcuts by searching for alpaquitay-ai.showMenu.

Does Alpaquitay send my code to an Alpaquitay server? No. There is no intermediary server. With a local provider your code never leaves the machine; with a cloud one it goes straight to that provider after the privacy boundary. The project's only server is the static model CDN, which only serves signed files and never receives your text. Is it free? Yes, the extension is free and open source (MIT). You only pay for what you use of a cloud provider, if you choose one. Do I need a GPU? Not to use Alpaquitay with Ollama, LM Studio or the cloud. Yes for the local engine (WebGPU). Can I use it on a company project? Yes. For confidential code, use local providers only and see the recipe Work without your code leaving your machine. Why does it ask so much before acting? On purpose: ask-before-act is one of its five principles. Short replies (si, si aplicar, no) make confirming take a second. Are the DORA metrics real? They are signals derived from Git and labelled as such. For operational metrics you need your deployment and incident data. Why are some messages and commands in Spanish? Alpaquitay was born in a Spanish-speaking community. The harness commands (deuda, si aplicar, promover…)
Alpaquitay AI is free software (MIT) made for the community. Every bit of help counts: a fix to this manual, a new use case, a well-described bug or a code improvement.

Every page ends with a Suggest an improvement to this page link that opens the Markdown file on GitHub for editing. The chapters are in docs/manual/en/ and the Spanish originals in docs/manual/es/, one file per chapter with the same number. If you change a chapter, change its translation too: the build fails when the two languages do not have the same chapters. Screenshots and videos are in manual/media/. The site is built with npm run manual:build, which fails on a broken link, a missing anchor or a missing image. npm run manual:check checks that the published copy is up to date. Style rules: short sentences, second person (you), one step per line in procedures, and nothing the extension does not really do. If you describe a feature, check it in the code or in the extension first.
